title: A woman remembered in poetry
summary: Beside Xiling Bridge, Mucai Pavilion commemorates Su Xiaoxiao, a woman whose name has travelled through poetry and local storytelling. The romantic details of her life are difficult to establish as history. This is a place to encounter literary memory: later generations kept imagining her, writing about her and remaking her memorial. What survives most clearly is her place in the cultural imagination of West Lake.

sections.heading: Memory is not a biography
sections.text: Hangzhou’s literary account describes Su Xiaoxiao’s life as difficult to reconstruct, and her image as something enlarged by generations of writers. The pavilion and memorial have also been rebuilt. Read them as a record of commemoration, rather than proof of every love story attached to the name. The standard place name is Xiling Bridge, 西泠桥.
